title: mySQL connections not returned to the pool when `fetch_optional` yields no results
body:
### Bug Description

When a query executed using `fetch_optional`returns no results, the connection is not returned to the pool. Once `max_connections` is exceeded all following connections fail with a `PoolTimedOut` error.

This seems to happen only when using the mySQL driver.

### Minimal Reproduction

To reproduce run this test:

```rust
#[tokio::test]
async fn mysql_test() {
    sqlx::any::install_default_drivers();

    let pool = sqlx::any::AnyPoolOptions::new()
        .max_connections(5)
        .connect_lazy("mysql://user:pass@localhost:3306/db")
        .unwrap();

    for i in 0..10 {
        println!("Query #{i} with results.");
        sqlx::query("SELECT 1 + 1")
            .fetch_optional(&pool)
            .await
            .unwrap();
    }

    for i in 0..10 {
        println!("Query #{i} without results.");
        sqlx::query("SELECT 1 + 1 WHERE 1=0")
            .fetch_optional(&pool)
            .await
            .unwrap();
    }
}
```

Which fails with a `PoolTimedOut` error:

```txt
running 1 test
Query #0 with results.
Query #1 with results.
Query #2 with results.
Query #3 with results.
Query #4 with results.
Query #5 with results.
Query #6 with results.
Query #7 with results.
Query #8 with results.
Query #9 with results.
Query #0 without results.
Query #1 without results.
Query #2 without results.
Query #3 without results.
Query #4 without results.
Query #5 without results.
thread 'mysql_test' panicked at 'called `Result::unwrap()` on an `Err` value: PoolTimedOut', tests/sql.rs:382:14
note: run with `RUST_BACKTRACE=1` environment variable to display a backtrace
test mysql_test ... FAILED
```

### Info
* SQLx version: 0.7.1
* SQLx features enabled: [ "runtime-tokio-rustls", "postgres", "mysql", "sqlite" ]
* Database server and version: 8.0.33 
* Operating system: MacOS and Linux
* `rustc --version`: rustc 1.70.0 (90c541806 2023-05-31)
